answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (PoroTomo DAS, Brady Hot Springs, March 2016; read-only report via report.py):

RECORDS AND ANOMALIES
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20; 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314% of the time span)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above the catalogue Mc)
- Pumping over 15.96 days: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 (net extraction)
- Catalogue (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016): 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07

CALIBRATED PROBABILITY (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5; LBNL catalogue magnitudes):
  b      Sigma      P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198      5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922       0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474        0.0006484                        0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated DAS magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Which is which: the per-b Sigma / P(M>=5.5) table above is the CALIBRATED estimate, because it is derived from the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue events with calibrated magnitudes. The single DAS-based number (b 0.9849, Sigma -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr 0.07842) is an UPPER BOUND only: DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and every DAS detection is counted as an event at/above Mc, so it over-counts events and sits well above the calibrated probabilities. On the calibrated numbers, a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is very unlikely (P/yr 1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 across b scenarios); even the over-counting DAS upper bound is ~7.8e-2 per year.
